title: She stayed… when others ran.
paragraphs:
Not loud.
Not famous.
Not powerful.
Few talk about devotion under pressure.

Because it is easy to follow Jesus when He is healing crowds…
When miracles are multiplying…
When hope feels like a rising tide.
But what about when everything collapses?
What about when following Him costs you everything?

The sky turns dark.
The crowd turns violent.
The Savior bleeds.
Silence from those who once said, “I will never leave You.”
But one woman steps closer instead of backing away.
And her presence at the cross is not random.
Many of us love Jesus… until it becomes uncomfortable.

We worship… until obedience costs us reputation.
We believe… until suffering enters the room.
We stay… until fear whispers louder than faith.
We don’t deny Him with our mouths…
But we abandon Him with our lives.
Because she knew what it felt like to be completely bound.
“Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out.”

Not one struggle.
Not a phase.
Not a small issue.
Some scholars interpret this as severe spiritual oppression—her life once consumed by darkness, identity shattered, dignity stripped, hope nearly erased.
And when Jesus sets you free from something that once owned you…
You don’t treat Him like an option.
Matthew 27:55–56 tells us she was there, watching the crucifixion.
John 19:25 says she stood near the cross.

Near the blood.
Near the suffering.
Near the shame.

The smell of iron in the air.
The sound of nails in wood.
The weight of a dying Savior.
Because grace had already rewritten her story.
Mary didn’t stay because she was fearless.
She stayed because she was redeemed.
And perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18).
Some of you are living a double life right now.
You haven’t denied Jesus with your lips…
But your choices are slowly creating distance.
Distance doesn’t feel like rebellion at first.
You realize you’re no longer near the cross.
Mary shows us something raw and real:
Those who have been deeply forgiven…
“Her many sins have been forgiven—as her great love has shown.”
Love is the evidence of forgiveness understood.
And then comes the moment that changes everything.
John 20:1 says Mary went to the tomb early, while it was still dark.

Even after all she saw…
Even after the cross…
She becomes the first witness of the risen Christ.
And here is the Gospel, clear and unfiltered:

We are all sinners (Romans 3:23).
We are all separated from God by sin (Isaiah 59:2).
We cannot save ourselves.
But Jesus Christ—the Son of God—came, lived without sin, and died on the cross for our sins (1 Peter 2:24).
He took the punishment we deserved.
And three days later, He rose again (1 Corinthians 15:3–4).
Through repentance and faith in Jesus alone (Ephesians 2:8–9).
You don’t have to stay bound.
You don’t have to keep running.
You don’t have to live divided.
But as someone who refuses to leave.

Bring your secrets.
Bring your shame.
Bring the parts of you no one else sees.
And He is not backing away.

Stay when it’s hard.
Stay when it costs you.
Stay when your feelings fluctuate.
Because the ones who stay through the cross…
Are the ones who witness resurrection.
